changes_outside_new_sources: The two release-week comparisons retained all original records and embeddings and introduced only the specified conference papers. On November 18 the registry and venue checks admitted zero new conference papers. Eighteen additional arXiv records became available and the candidate sets changed. The revised grouping omitted the specific candidate whose earlier review failed. The extra rank used three previously collected preprints.

selection_review.editorial_judgment: The headline and short summary extend the same resource-management latency bound to all three papers. BRUMM measures the time to reclaim memory in L4Re and accounts for it with a quota. MPORA measures deadline attainment and job response time with SPEC workloads and uses probabilistic prediction intervals. PREEMPT-FaaS measures controller and service times under Kubernetes and Knative load. Their experiments concern three different operations. Each paper supplies evidence for its own performance measure.

selection_review.audit_changes: The audit regenerated the English reader with the scoped note. All ranked entries and every stored original article, embedding and topic file matched the scientific run.

exclusions_reviewed.question_checked: Security and timing in embedded systems
exclusions_reviewed.reason: The four studies evaluate different properties of operating systems, schedulers and networks. Their timing or security measurements use different units and success criteria. The four evaluations use different workloads and endpoints.

The processor study compares worst-case execution-time estimates with a handcrafted model. The partitioning experiment counts workable configurations on an ARM platform. The automotive study measures utilization and design stability. The event-scheduling study measures the share of schedulable task sets and the scheduling runtime. The hypervisor study derives response-time bounds. The related timing vocabulary does not identify one endpoint shared by three studies.

A six-person simulator study recorded brain activity and perceived workload. A review compared the protocols of 80 vehicle-interaction studies. The stimulus-selection paper compares confusion matrices for sounds and vibration patterns. These are three different questions and units of observation.

exclusions_reviewed.question_checked: Virtual-reality notation, navigation and collision prevention
exclusions_reviewed.reason: The navigation study compares travel through a three-dimensional timeline. The notation study asked six researchers and six industry practitioners to describe viewpoints in a collaborative setting. The collision-prevention study observed approaches to a physical boundary and surveyed presence. None of the three tasks measures the performance of the other two.

The same two authors analyzed 66 nonvisual STEM interface studies for architectural features and 17 accessibility systems for user verification. The separate virtual-reality study observed six teams of three participants performing a collaborative task. The first two studies share authors, and the third measures team behavior.

interpretation.selection_scope: Every rank with a new proceedings paper and every wholly excluded proposed group with at least two new proceedings papers. Grouping measures overlap in the trials. A paper outside a proposed group cannot enter the ranking.
interpretation.limits: One systems rank and three excluded HCI candidates do not establish field-wide editorial quality. A stored enrichment fallback affected one HCI notation paper. Its original abstract and bibliography were available to the independent review. Neither information-science journal supplied a ranked paper on these three dates. Additional systems and HCI publication weeks and library-science evidence are still required before promotion.

cost_usd.basis: Differences of stored cumulative model ledgers. Only the two fresh baselines and three restored comparisons are new charges. Audit and source checks added zero ledger spend. Fees exclude hosting and staff time.
